text:
The light filtering through the grimy window of the Blackwood Bay Chronicle office wasn't right. It had a bleached, almost clinical quality, like the fluorescent glow of a forgotten waiting room, making the familiar dust motes dance with an unsettling pallor. Outside, the air itself felt thin, scrubbed clean of scent, leaving behind only the distant, hollow clang of the shipyard and the ceaseless, low thrum that seemed to emanate from the very bedrock of the town. Vance stared at the framed photo on his desk – a missing person flyer, already faded at the edges. Another one.

He was mid-sentence in his notes, detailing a local councilman's oddly evasive answers about the old lighthouse acquisition, when the tremor hit. It wasn't violent, not even a shake, more a deep, resonant hum that travelled up from the floorboards, rattling the cheap ceramic mug on his desk just enough to make the cold coffee slosh. A fresh hairline crack traced itself across the plaster ceiling above his head, an intricate vein branching from an older scar. The thrumming subsided, leaving the quiet heavier than before, pregnant with unspoken things. Blackwood Bay always had a way of shifting beneath your feet, whether you noticed it or not.
